archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A thick-framed creator who holds the ball, absorbs pressure and wins as often off-script with his legs as he does from the pocket; his rushing value comes from scrambles, not designed runs.

report.headline: Two-game sample shows growth, but the hamstring stalls it until mid-October
report.take:
Williams is a hold-it-and-create quarterback, and two seasons in that identity is settled. He has finished 7th in QB rushing yards both years, and this season 10 of his 70 dropbacks became scrambles, worth 0.914 EPA apiece and six first downs. The designed runs don't work: five of them produced -0.553 EPA with a 60% stuff rate. His legs pay off when the pocket breaks down, not as a called part of the run game. Time to throw has climbed from 2.92 as a rookie to 3.20 last year to 3.42 now. That's the cost of how he plays, and the bill shows up as pressure: he was pressured on 40% of dropbacks, the highest rate among the 32 tracked passers.

The interesting part is what happens once pressure arrives. As a rookie, 43.5% of his pressures became sacks, 60th of 63. Under Ben Johnson in 2025 that fell to 15.9%, 5th-best, and this year's 20.8% (9th) says the change held. The 8.3% sack rate ranks 30th, but that comes from how often he's under siege, not from freezing in the pocket. His bad-throw rate is also down to 10.9% from roughly 18% in both prior seasons. Over 55 attempts that's a hint rather than proof, but it points the same direction as a +5.5 CPOE from a passer who was at -3.5 last year.

The headline efficiency, 0.292 EPA per dropback (7th), comes almost entirely from one game. In the Week 1 shootout at Carolina he went 21 of 29 with +18.6 pass EPA and a +16.6 CPOE. Against Minnesota, today's top-ranked defense, he was pressured 40.6% of the time, blitzed 21 times, threw at a 3.9-yard intended air depth and finished at -1.0 EPA in a 9-3 loss. Other numbers will come down too: 58.8% third-down conversions at 8.3 yards to go, and +0.682 EPA on seven deep attempts. The truer picture sits between the two games: an improving, efficient-when-protected passer whose floor drops sharply against fronts that can get home.

For now, all of that is on hold. A hamstring strain has kept him out since Week 2. Case Keenum started Weeks 3 and 4, and the team's own reported return estimate is October 18, which puts Week 6 as the earliest realistic target. When he comes back, it will be without left tackle Braxton Jones, who is on IR until early November. For a quarterback already facing the most pressure in the league, that is the most important supporting-cast fact on the page.

strengths.title: Pressure no longer becomes sacks
strengths.body: The jump from a 43.5% pressure-to-sack rate as a rookie to 15.9% in 2025 and 20.8% this year is the defining change of the Johnson era. He still extends plays, but he now gets the ball out or escapes instead of going down. Because it has held across a full season and into this one, it looks like learned behavior rather than noise.

strengths.title: Scrambles are a real chain-mover
strengths.body: Scrambles account for 14.3% of his dropbacks, and they've produced 86 yards and six first downs at nearly a point of EPA each. Paired with consecutive 7th-place finishes in QB rushing, this is a stable fantasy floor that survives bad passing days. In the Minnesota game he still ran for 42 yards while the passing game sank.

strengths.title: Cleaner ball placement
strengths.body: He is completing passes at 5.5 points over expected, against -3.5 last year, and his bad-throw rate is down to 10.9% from 17.8%. The sample is 55 attempts, so expect some of it to fade. Even so, it fits the trend of a quarterback in his second year with the same play-caller.

concerns.title: Hamstring timeline, then a thinner line
concerns.body: He is out and classified week-to-week, with an estimated return of October 18, so a reaggravation could push that back. When he does return, starting left tackle Braxton Jones (65% of snaps) will be on IR into November. A hamstring also threatens the scramble game that drives his value, at least in his first games back.

concerns.title: Most-pressured QB in the league
concerns.body: A 40% pressure rate ranks last among 32 qualifiers. Part of that is his style: a 3.42-second time to throw invites it. The Minnesota game shows what happens when a good front gets home. His intended air yards collapsed to 3.9 and the offense scored three points.

concerns.title: Efficiency built on one shootout
concerns.body: His 7th-ranked EPA per dropback leans on a Carolina game that finished 59-37. Several hot splits will cool: seven deep attempts at +0.682 EPA and third-down conversions at 58.8%. His 2025 per-play EPA of 0.086 (27th) is a more honest starting point than this two-game line.

trend.note: In two games he went from 37.3 PPR and +18.6 pass EPA in a Week 1 shootout to 7.7 PPR against the league's top defense. Since then he has missed two starts with the hamstring.

nextGame.headline: Ruled out: a soft Packers defense goes to Keenum
nextGame.body:
On paper Green Bay suits him. The Packers rank 26th in defensive EPA and 24th against the pass, and they allow a +0.901 EPA on deep throws (23rd). They limit explosive passes well (4th) and have held quarterbacks to 220 yards a game (6th fewest), so this is a defense that gives up efficiency underneath rather than shot plays. Williams himself is not expected to be part of it. He is Out, isn't practicing this week, and has an estimated return a week after this game.

On the Chicago side, the relevant facts are Keenum making a third straight start and Braxton Jones's absence at left tackle. Green Bay's report is heavier. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (83% of snaps) is lost for the season, Micah Parsons has yet to play and is out again, and starting corner Brandon Cisse (90%) is questionable with a neck injury. On offense the Packers are without center Jacob Monk (96%). Their offense already ranks 32nd in rush EPA and 31st in hit rate allowed, which sets up Chicago's 2nd-ranked pass defense and 4th-ranked sack rate.

keyMatchups.title: Bears pass rush vs. depleted Packers line
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay's quarterback is hit on 20.4% of dropbacks, the second-worst rate in the league, and now loses its starting center. Chicago sacks quarterbacks on 8.6% of dropbacks, 4th in the league. This is the matchup most likely to decide the game whoever starts at quarterback for Chicago.

keyMatchups.title: Packers back seven without Cooper
keyMatchups.body: Losing an every-down linebacker hurts a defense that already ranks 24th in success rate allowed. That should help Chicago's short and intermediate game even with Keenum throwing.

keyMatchups.title: Green Bay's broken run game
keyMatchups.body: The Packers' offense ranks dead last in rush EPA. That leaves them leaning on passing against Chicago's 2nd-ranked pass defense, and a low-scoring, Bears-controlled script is the likeliest shape for this game.

nextGame.watch: Whether Williams returns to any practice late in the week. Full participation would point to a Week 6 return; another week of no practice would put his October 18 estimate in doubt.

restOfSeason.body:
Assuming he returns around Week 6, expect something closer to his 2025 level, with modest gains rather than the Week 1 version. The ball-security change under pressure and the scramble production have held across seasons, so they are durable. A CPOE above +5 and the deep and third-down efficiency should come back toward average. Chicago's run lean (23rd in pass rate over expected) and a top-five defense cap his passing volume, so his fantasy value will keep depending on 25-40 rushing yards a week.

The main risk is protection. Jones is out until November and Williams already faces the most pressure in the league. The first few games back could also come with a quarterback reluctant to scramble on a healing hamstring, and that takes away his best counter to pressure.
swingFactors: Hamstring recovery and willingness to scramble
Left-tackle play until Braxton Jones returns
Whether the lower bad-throw rate holds over a larger sample

bets.reason: Chicago has won with Keenum starting, including 23-12 over the Jets, and its defense ranks 5th in EPA. Green Bay ranks 26th in both offensive and defensive EPA and is missing its center and an every-down linebacker. A field goal is a modest number given that gap.

Green Bay's offense ranks 32nd in rush EPA and 31st in hit rate allowed, facing Chicago's 2nd-ranked pass defense. Chicago runs more than situation predicts, with a backup at quarterback. The Bears' one game with Keenum whose score we have finished at 35 total points.

confidence.note: Two-game sample split between a shootout and the top defense; currently out with an open-ended hamstring timeline.
